message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $382 and am on CHANCE. My pink and orange monopolies are fully built with two and four houses respectively. The other players hold red properties with three to four houses each, plus an unmortgaged Boardwalk.

Player four has yellow properties with one to two houses and an unmortgaged Med. The bank has no houses left, so I will not buy hotels. My $382 cash buffer protects me from the $360 rent on Marvin Gardens.

Standard Monopoly rent tables show my previous orange and pink estimates were wrong. I will rely on the game's prior notes for accurate figures.

Turn 108 notes confirm the game's orange 4-house rent is $750/$750/$800. This matches the pink table, so the prior rent confusion is resolved.

Player two has $395 and could spend $300 to upgrade their red properties to four houses each. The strategic principle remains sound even if the exact rent figures are uncertain.

Player four has $276 and could buy a yellow house to raise Marvin Gardens from two to three houses. That would push rent to $850, which I cannot afford without selling assets. Unmortgaging would also shrink my cash buffer below the current $360 rent. Hoteling one orange property is under consideration, though it returns four houses to the bank.

Hoteling one orange property costs $200, leaving $182 in cash. Player two can spend $300 to build two red houses and reach four houses each on their reds.

Player four can only buy one yellow house because they have $276. Under even-building rules, that house must go on Atlantic or Ventnor, not on Marvin Gardens. Marvin would stay at two houses and rent would remain $360. Hoteling an orange property would not force a higher rent from player four.

Hoteling an orange property would return four houses to the bank. Player two could then spend $300 to upgrade their red properties to four houses each, raising red rent to $1050–$1100 and likely bankrupting me. Selling houses is equally dangerous because it returns them to the bank for opponents to buy. Unmortgaging any property would cost more than its rent and shrink my cash buffer below the $360 needed to cover Marvin Gardens.

I am evaluating trade options. Player two holds an unmortgaged Boardwalk and mortgaged Pacific and Penn, while player four owns a mortgaged Park Place. Neither player holds a dark blue monopoly. I could try to acquire Park Place from player four in exchange for something else.

I do not need Boardwalk, and trading my two Get Out of Jail Free cards for cash would be unwise. I will end this turn and keep the housing lock.
